Definition: Percentage of national population with access to electricity (grid or off-grid). This is the primary indicator of energy infrastructure availability for ICT. Based on World Bank/IEA Tracking SDG7 data, national statistical offices, or Afrobarometer surveys.
revision_notes: The cited source (data.worldbank.org/country/congo-dem-rep) is the World Bank country page for the Democratic Republic of Congo, not the Republic of Congo (COG) — a country mismatch, and the 22.1% figure it implies belongs to DRC, not COG. World Bank SDG7/electrification tracking data for the Republic of Congo (WB_SE4ALL_EG_ACS_ELEC indicator) show electricity access at 51.3% of the population in 2023, up from 50.6% in 2022, consistently reported across TradingEconomics and TheGlobalEconomy.com as reproductions of the same World Bank series. 51.3% falls in the 50-74% band, raising the code from 1 to 3.
revised_comments: World Bank data show 51.3% of the population in the Republic of Congo had access to electricity in 2023, up marginally from 50.6% in 2022. Access is highly uneven: around 67% of the urban population is connected against just 12.4% in rural areas, reflecting the concentration of grid infrastructure around Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire.

Definition: Frequency and severity of power outages experienced by businesses and households. Based on World Bank Enterprise Surveys, Afrobarometer, or national utility data. Reflects the quality of electricity supply beyond mere access — critical for running ICT equipment and data infrastructure.
Value Name: Severe (frequent daily outages or regular load shedding)
Comments: Severe outages implied by low access
revision_notes: The originally cited Afrobarometer article is a 39-country pan-African round-up that does not isolate Congo-specific outage figures; the 'Severe' rating rested on an inference from the (mismatched) access-rate row rather than direct outage evidence. The World Bank Enterprise Surveys 2024 country profile for Congo, Rep. (fieldwork March-October 2024, 365 firms) provides direct firm-level evidence: 77.1% of firms experienced electrical outages in the previous fiscal year, averaging 9.0 outages per month — both worse than the Sub-Saharan Africa average (72.1% of firms, 7.6 outages/month). This directly supports a 'Severe' rating (near-weekly-to-twice-weekly outages affecting the large majority of firms), confirming the original code of 1 on stronger, country-specific grounds.
revised_comments: World Bank Enterprise Survey data for 2024 show that 77.1% of formal firms in the Republic of Congo experienced power outages in the previous fiscal year, with an average of 9.0 outages per month — worse than both the Sub-Saharan Africa average (72.1% of firms, 7.6 outages/month) and the Lower Middle Income country average. This points to a severe and widespread grid reliability problem affecting the great majority of businesses.
